a.speaker: The lantern meeting
a.text:
Day {day}. Eleven households in Ruth's garage, one lantern, too many opinions. Water first: the taps {tap_state}. Then food, then who watches the street at night.

Everyone keeps looking at you. Some of that is Trust. Some of it is Profile.

options.text: Lay It Out: with three households already behind you, propose a common pantry and a watch rota.
effects: M2: Common Pantry. The street pools its food and keeps a night watch. Cohesion +2.

options.text: Propose a common pantry and a watch rota.
Build rain catchment off every downspout on the court.
effects: M2: rain catchment on the court, 22 water-days stored.

options.text: Offer the Achterbergs' farmhouse well your fuel for its hand pump: a well share.
effects: M2: Well Share. Ten gallons a month from the Achterberg well.

options.text: Tell them about the Guard water point on Cornell Road.
effects: M2: the street walks to the Guard water point.

options.text: Keep quiet. Your family's stores are your family's.

no_pantry.speaker: The lantern meeting
no_pantry.text: It falls apart over whose freezer counts. Nobody leaves angry, but nobody leaves agreed. Try another way, or go it alone.

options.text: Fall back on the catchment idea.

pantry.speaker: Ruth Pellow
pantry.text:
Ruth writes it on the back of a calendar: who gives what, who watches when. "I ran a dispatch board for thirty-one years," she says. "I can run a pantry."

Common Pantry: the court shares food and keeps a watch. It is the first step toward a Court Charter.

catch.speaker: The lantern meeting
catch.text: By Day 6 every downspout on the court runs into a barrel or a trash can. November in the valley is wet; for once that's good news.

well.speaker: Hank Achterberg
well.text: "Pump's from 1952. Never needed power in its life." Ten gallons a month for your fuel, and a farmhouse that knows your name.

guard.speaker: The lantern meeting
guard.text: The Talbert Guard runs a water point at the Cornell Road fire station: a hardened pump, two soldiers, a census clipboard. They want names. They give water.

alone.speaker: The lantern meeting
alone.text: You say little and leave early. By the next night, the whole court has decided what it thinks your garage holds.
